originalTitle: Archer-Daniels Stock is Trading at 15 Times Forward Earnings. Is that Cheap?

content:
Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (NYSE: ADM ) has had a great year, with the stock surging almost 32%, compared with the S&P 500's 15% return. Earnings have started to recover, and investors have noticed. The stock is up as well. That leaves investors with a fairly simple question: after the recovery, is ADM still reasonably valued?

ADM's Biggest Advantage Is Its Scale

Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (NYSE:ADM) does not have the kind of moat that comes from owning brands people see on grocery store shelves. Its advantage is much less visible. The company has built a huge network spanning agricultural origination, transportation, processing, biofuels, food ingredients, and nutrition. That gives ADM the ability to move commodities through different parts of the supply chain and make money from several stages of the process.

The benefit of that scale showed up in the latest results. In Q2 2026, operating profit from Ag Services & Oilseeds jumped 129% from a year earlier. Carbohydrate Solutions and Nutrition were up 22% and 51%, respectively. ADM also pointed to its global asset network as an advantage in dealing with a complicated agricultural market. There is a catch, though. This is still a cyclical business. ADM's margins can move around quite a bit depending on crop prices, energy costs, trade policies, and biofuel markets. So while the company's scale gives it an edge, it does not make the business immune to industry cycles.

Archer-Daniels-Midland Company (NYSE:ADM) looks expensive if you only look at its trailing P/E. At around $80.45 a share, the stock trades at roughly 22 times trailing earnings, based on diluted EPS of about $3.66. However, that number doesn't tell the whole story. ADM expects earnings to improve significantly in 2026. The company raised its adjusted EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.60, up from $4.15-$4.70 previously. Using the midpoint of the new guidance, ADM is trading at roughly 15 times 2026 adjusted earnings.

That is a pretty big difference. Investors are not necessarily paying 22 times earnings because they think ADM's current earnings are worth that much. They are looking past the weaker trailing results and betting that the recovery continues. At about 15 times expected earnings, the valuation looks much more reasonable.

But ADM Isn't as Cheap as It Used to Be

The problem is that ADM's current forward P/E is already toward the higher end of its recent range. ADM's forward P/E was around 15.0x in 2025, 10.9x in 2024, 11.0x in 2023, 14.1x in 2022, and 14.5x in 2021. At roughly 15x today, investors are paying more than they did in several of those years. That doesn't automatically make ADM expensive. However, it does tell us something important: the market has already priced in a decent part of the earnings recovery. If earnings keep improving, the valuation could prove reasonable. If the recovery loses steam, the stock has less of a cushion.

Moreover, ADM isn't the cheapest stock in its peer group. ADM's valuation looks fairly reasonable next to some competitors, but there are cheaper options. Recent estimates put ADM's forward P/E in the mid-teens. Ingredion and Bunge, for example, trade closer to 11x-12x forward earnings, while Darling Ingredients is around 13x-17x depending on the estimates being used. ADM can command a premium. Its scale is difficult to replicate, and its operations are spread across several parts of the agricultural and food supply chain. Its long dividend history also makes it attractive to a different group of investors. Still, a 15x multiple isn't a screaming bargain when some similar businesses are available at lower prices.

The dividend is another reason investors may be willing to stick with ADM. The company recently increased its quarterly dividend to $0.52 per share. That marked its 53rd consecutive year of dividend growth, while ADM has paid an uninterrupted dividend for more than 94 years. At $80.45 a share, that works out to an annual dividend of $2.08 and a yield of about 2.6%. A 2.6% yield won't turn many heads on its own. The appeal is really in the combination of the yield, the long history of increases, and the potential for earnings to recover. ADM has a long dividend-growth record, but it may not be the only rising dividend stock worth a closer look. See which other names stand out in 11 Best Rising Dividend Stocks to Buy Right Now .

Of course, the company still has to balance the dividend with the money it needs to invest back into the business. The earnings recovery is what matters for now. For ADM, the next leg of the story comes down to earnings. The company's 2026 outlook is tied to several moving pieces, including biofuel economics, renewable fuel obligations, energy prices, and margins in crushing and ethanol. Management also expects the Nutrition business to keep improving.

If those trends continue, ADM could earn more than investors currently expect. If that happens, today's 15x forward P/E would look a lot less demanding. However, things can go the other way. A weaker agricultural market, lower processing margins, poor ethanol economics, or unfavorable trade policies could put pressure on earnings. If estimates come down, that 15x forward P/E would suddenly look less attractive.

Earnings Don't Tell the Whole Story

ADM's cash flow is worth watching too. The company generated $1.30 billion in operating cash flow during the first half of 2026 and spent $466 million on capital expenditures. That leaves about $833 million after capital spending, before dividends and other financing needs.

Cash generation has improved as earnings have recovered, but ADM is not a light-asset business. It expects to spend between $1.3 billion and $1.5 billion on capital expenditures for all of 2026. So investors shouldn't look at a 15x earnings multiple in isolation. ADM still needs to put a meaningful amount of money back into its operations. chineseTitle: 阿彻丹尼尔斯股票的交易价格是预期市盈率的 15 倍。便宜吗？
chineseSummary: 阿彻-丹尼尔斯-米德兰公司 (NYSE:ADM) 度过了美好的一年，其股价飙升近 32%，而标准普尔 500 指数的回报率为 15%。盈利已经开始复苏，投资者已经注意到了。股票也涨了。这给投资者留下了一个相当简单的问题：复苏后，ADM 的估值是否仍然合理？ ADM 的最大优势 [...]
chineseContent:
阿彻-丹尼尔斯-米德兰公司（纽约证券交易所代码：ADM）今年表现出色，其股价飙升近 32%，而标准普尔 500 指数的回报率为 15%。盈利已经开始复苏，投资者已经注意到了。股票也涨了。这给投资者留下了一个相当简单的问题：复苏后，ADM 的估值是否仍然合理？

ADM最大的优势是规模

阿彻丹尼尔斯米德兰公司（纽约证券交易所股票代码：ADM）并不拥有人们在杂货店货架上看到的自有品牌的护城河。它的优势不太明显。该公司建立了涵盖农业起源、运输、加工、生物燃料、食品配料和营养的庞大网络。这使得 ADM 能够在供应链的不同部分运输商品，并从流程的多个阶段赚钱。

这种规模的好处体现在最新的结果中。 2026 年第二季度，农业服务和油籽业务的营业利润同比增长 129%。碳水化合物解决方案和营养品分别增长 22% 和 51%。 ADM还指出，其全球资产网络是应对复杂农业市场的优势。不过，有一个问题。这仍然是一个周期性业务。 ADM 的利润率可能会根据农作物价格、能源成本、贸易政策和生物燃料市场而大幅波动。因此，尽管该公司的规模赋予其优势，但这并不能使其业务免受行业周期的影响。

如果您只看其追踪市盈率，阿彻丹尼尔斯米德兰公司（纽约证券交易所股票代码：ADM）看起来很昂贵。该股每股约 80.45 美元，基于约 3.66 美元的摊薄后每股收益，其交易价格约为往绩市盈率的 22 倍。然而，这个数字并不能说明全部情况。 ADM 预计 2026 年盈利将大幅改善。该公司将调整后每股收益指引从之前的 4.15-4.70 美元上调至 5.15-5.60 美元。根据新指引的中值，ADM 的交易价格约为 2026 年调整后收益的 15 倍。

这是一个相当大的差异。投资者不一定会支付 22 倍的市盈率，因为他们认为 ADM 当前的盈利值这么多钱。他们正在忽略较弱的跟踪业绩，并押注复苏将持续。预期市盈率约为15倍，估值看起来更为合理。

但 ADM 并不像以前那么便宜

问题在于，ADM 目前的远期市盈率已经接近其近期范围的高端。 ADM 的远期市盈率在 2025 年约为 15.0 倍，2024 年为 10.9 倍，2023 年为 11.0 倍，2022 年为 14.1 倍，2021 年为 14.5 倍。如今，投资者支付的市盈率约为 15 倍，比过去几年要高。这不会自动使 ADM 变得昂贵。然而，它确实告诉我们一些重要的事情：市场已经消化了盈利复苏的很大一部分。如果盈利持续改善，估值可能是合理的。如果复苏失去动力，该股的缓冲就会减少。

此外，ADM 并不是同类股票中最便宜的股票。与一些竞争对手相比，ADM 的估值看起来相当合理，但还有更便宜的选择。最近的估计显示 ADM 的远期市盈率在十几岁左右。例如，Ingredion 和 Bunge 的预期收益接近 11 倍至 12 倍，而 Darling Ingredients 的预期收益约为 13 倍至 17 倍，具体取决于所使用的估计。 ADM 可以收取溢价。其规模难以复制，其业务分布在农业和食品供应链的多个部分。其悠久的股息历史也使其对不同的投资者群体具有吸引力。尽管如此，当一些类似的企业以更低的价格出售时，15 倍的市盈率并不是一个令人尖叫的便宜货。

股息是投资者愿意坚持持有 ADM 的另一个原因。该公司最近将季度股息提高至每股 0.52 美元。这标志着其股息连续第 53 年增长，而 ADM 已连续支付股息超过 94 年。按每股 80.45 美元计算，年度股息为 2.08 美元，收益率约为 2.6%。 2.6%的收益率本身不会引起很多人的注意。其吸引力实际上在于收益率、长期增长历史以及盈利恢复潜力的结合。 ADM 有着长期的股息增长记录，但它可能不是唯一值得仔细关注的股息上涨股票。看看还有哪些名字在 11 只值得立即购买的最佳股息上涨股票中脱颖而出。

当然，公司仍然必须平衡股息与投资回业务所需的资金。目前最重要的是盈利复苏。对于 ADM 来说，故事的下一步归结为收益。该公司 2026 年的前景与几个动态因素相关，包括生物燃料经济、可再生燃料义务、能源价格以及压榨和乙醇的利润率。管理层还预计营养业务将不断改善。

如果这些趋势持续下去，ADM 的盈利可能会超出投资者目前的预期。如果发生这种情况，今天 15 倍的远期市盈率看起来就不会那么苛刻了。然而，事情也可能朝相反的方向发展。农业市场疲软、加工利润率下降、乙醇经济状况不佳或不利的贸易政策可能会给盈利带来压力。如果预期下降，15 倍的远期市盈率就会突然显得不那么有吸引力。

盈利并不能说明全部情况

ADM的现金流也值得关注。该公司在 2026 年上半年产生了 13 亿美元的运营现金流，并花费了 4.66 亿美元的资本支出。除去资本支出、股息和其他融资需求之前，还剩下约 8.33 亿美元。

随着盈利的恢复，现金产生能力有所改善，但 ADM 并不是轻资产业务。该公司预计 2026 年全年的资本支出将在 13 亿至 15 亿美元之间。因此，投资者不应孤立地看待 15 倍的市盈率。 ADM 仍然需要将大量资金重新投入运营。 ADM 并不是唯一一家值得关注现金生成的公司。投资者寻找
